initialSix.interpretation: Both complete native touch wins passed immediately. Four ancillary failures required fixture-versus-production diagnosis.

fixtureCorrections: Partial touchEnd initially submitted remaining contacts and released the wrong finger; touchMove with a subset did not lift a contact. The final adapter submits the lifted contact and requires its actual trusted pointerup ID before continuing.
An exact lock-progress assertion after release wrongly disallowed natural decay; corrected to require no increase.
A second-finger Pause gesture did not promise native click synthesis. The Pause control is tested with a genuine single-touch tap.

Headless tab activation and native window minimization left document visibility visible, even after disabling Playwright focus emulation. This is not an app failure or a native-hidden acceptance claim.

confirmedProductionFailures.problem: Last-written interaction pointer discarded another still-held contact.
confirmedProductionFailures.reproduction: At the reachable steady lock, contacts 16 and 17 touched Hold to interact. A verified trusted pointerup 17 lifted only the newer contact. Lock progress fell from 15% to 10% over 800 ms while contact 16 remained held.
confirmedProductionFailures.receiptNote: The final pointercancel 16 is test cleanup after the failed assertion, not the user lifting the held contact.
confirmedProductionFailures.correction: Use per-pointer Set ownership; matching up/cancel/lostcapture removes only that contact and lifecycle release clears all.

confirmedProductionFailures.problem: Native finger drift could hand the interaction gesture to page panning.
confirmedProductionFailures.reproduction: A trusted interaction touch moved 24 CSS px vertically; Chromium emitted trusted pointercancel to #interact and lock progress was 0% after 4,200 ms instead of 100%.
confirmedProductionFailures.correction: Apply touch-action: none and user-select: none to the interaction control.

green: Both confirmed symptoms passed unchanged meaningful acceptance assertions against the corrected production build.
